# Six guides describe the Sass theme sources that 14.0 removes

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context

#21217 (PR #21225) turns the engine's theme sources into plain CSS: `resources/scss/**/*.scss` becomes `resources/css/**/*.css`, the theme build copies the sheets instead of compiling them, Sass leaves the engine, and a package names its sheets with `"neo": {"css": "<dir>"}` instead of `"neo": {"scss": "<dir>"}`. Its Contract Ledger leaves the guides to a follow-up leaf. This is that leaf.

## The Problem

Six files under `learn/` still describe the Sass tree on `dev`: `guides/uibuildingblocks/StylingAndTheming.md` (25 mentions: the theme tree, file paths, "built with SCSS"), `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsStyling.md` (2), and `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts.md`, `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsAdoption.md`, `guides/fundamentals/CodebaseOverview.md` and `tutorials/Earthquakes.md` (1 each). Once #21217 merges, a reader who follows them looks for files that no longer exist.

## The Architectural Reality

- Theme sources: `resources/css/{src,theme-*}/**/*.css`, one file per class per theme, plain CSS with native nesting. The built output and its URLs do not change: `dist/<env>/css/<folder>/<class>.css`, mapped by `resources/theme-map.json`.
- A workspace keeps its own sheets in `resources/css`; a package names its root with `"neo": {"css": "<dir>"}`.
- `buildScripts/build/themes.mjs` copies the sources through postcss (autoprefixer, plus cssnano for esm and production).
- The motion vocabulary is declared once in `src/Global.css`, for every `neo-theme-*` root.

## The Fix

Rewrite each mention to the plain-CSS tree: `resources/scss/…/*.scss` becomes `resources/css/…/*.css`, and "SCSS" becomes "CSS". Any Sass-only syntax a guide shows (variables, mixins, `@import`, `//` comments) becomes its plain-CSS form: custom properties, nesting, block comments. Where `StylingAndTheming.md` explains how a theme is built, it describes the copy build and the package field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git grep -niE "resources/scss|\.scss\b|\bsass\b" -- learn ':!learn/blog'` prints nothing.
- [ ] Every path the six files name exists on `dev` after #21217 has merged.
- [ ] `StylingAndTheming.md` describes the copy build and the `"neo": {"css": "<dir>"}` field.

## Out of Scope

Blog posts under `learn/blog/` (they describe their own time) · release notes · the generated workspace's scaffold (neomjs/create-app#61) · the engine change itself (#21217).

## Avoided Traps

- **Editing before #21217 merges.** The guides would then name files that do not exist yet; this ticket is blocked by #21217.

- 2026-11-17T14:02:37Z @tobiu referenced in commit `1cc7576` - "feat(themes): the theme sources become plain CSS, and the theme build copies them (#21217) (#21225)

* feat(themes): convert the theme sources to plain CSS with a proving converter (#21217)

buildScripts/helpers/convertScssToCss.mjs writes resources/css from resources/scss and
compiles both to prove each pair equal. At 825047c9ea: 722 of 722 files identical; 720
converted, 2 compiled (D4), 15 flattened in place (D2/D3), the D3 negative control (Euclid's
shorthand falsifier, #18182 comment 19670346) passing. Flattening replaces lifting single
rules, which reordered them against their siblings (#18182 comment 19670216).

Beyond the Discussion's rules, the compiled files keep their comments, adjacent line
comments become one block, and each block that Sass shared and the conversion copies
names its other copies.

Equality under Sass cannot see where Sass reads more leniently than a browser, so every
declaration value is also probed through Sass and Sass's reading is adopted where it differs
(custom properties and CSS math functions exempt). One case on this tree: the trailing comma
in Range's `input[type=range]::-moz-range-track,` selector, which Sass drops and a browser
rejects with the whole rule.

The build still compiles resources/scss until the next commit.

* feat(themes): the theme build and watcher copy plain CSS instead of compiling Sass (#21217)

build-themes and watch-themes read resources/css. Every .css file is a class sheet, copied
through autoprefixer (plus cssnano for esm and production) with a source map back to it.
A package declares its root as "neo": {"css": "<dir>"}. With no partials left, the
watcher's partial freshness boundaries, root-forced rebuilds and Sass preload go.

Measured against a Sass build of 825047c9ea in a worktree:
- theme-map.json is byte-identical (AC-4);
- development: 722 of 722 sheets identical once flattened through Sass;
- esm and production: 720 of 722 sheets hold the same declarations per context and
  selector, in the same override order; the other two differ only where cssnano kept
  `center` for `50%` in one background-position and where one identical declaration is
  duplicated.

* refactor(themes): one authority for the blocks the conversion copied (#21217)

The motion vocabulary moves from five per-theme copies into src/Global.css, declared once
for every element carrying a neo-theme-* class, workspace and package themes included;
_motion.scss had called a per-theme copy a divergence trap. No other rule declares a motion
token, so moving it from the theme roots to one zero-specificity rule changes no computed
value. Without the nested @media, the theme Globals no longer need D3's flattening and
read as their sources did.

The design-token sheets and global/MouseCursor were copied into their Global sheets and
also built on their own, though no class asks for the standalone files. They go, and the
copies in the Global sheets are the authority. convertDesignTokens.mjs goes with them: it
wrote the files that no longer exist, and its output predates the hand edits since
(#18747), which a run would have reverted.

The converter gains a working-tree mode (ref `.`), and Sass's re-indented comments align
again. The tree is the converter's output for the base plus these source edits: 715 of
715 files equal.

* refactor(themes): every reader of the theme sources reads resources/css; resources/scss goes (#21217)

Scaffolders, lints, the class-move tooling, the CI scope classifier, contributor standing,
the e2e spec reach, the webpack resource copy, the lint-staged key, 20 test files and 15
source comments follow the plain-CSS tree:
- create/scss.mjs becomes create/css.mjs and writes .css stubs; create/theme.mjs parses
  with postcss and only retargets the theme class (no Sass module paths to rebase).
- moveStyleTransforms rewrites a moved sheet's relative CSS @import URLs, the one
  module reference plain CSS has; the move specs prove it with an @import bundle.
- check-theme-value-files and check-theme-surfaces drop their Sass-only comment and
  interpolation handling; check-theme-coverage drops the `global` row, a package that no
  longer exists.
- test/playwright/util/flattenCss.mjs reads nesting the browser way for the two specs that
  compiled with Sass to get flat selectors; it agrees with Sass on 715 of 715 sheets.

The converter gains three checks, each found by a reading Sass could not make:
- a second equality arm through flattenCss, with no Sass leniency;
- Sass nested properties expand to their longhands (References.css `background: {…}`,
  which a browser drops whole);
- Sass imports, placeholders and @at-root/@content left in output fail the run.
D4 now flattens only the top-level nodes holding control flow or an `&-suffix`, in place:
dashboard/Container.css keeps 32 of its 43 nodes as authored. Proof at 825047c9ea: 722 of
722 equal in both readings; the final tree: 715 of 715.

Comments that still spoke Sass (`@use`, mixins, `_motion.scss`, "the shared SCSS") now
state the plain-CSS fact, and DockRailRevealRetarget says its four keyframe pairs are
hand-written twins now, kept by its own arm.

* build(themes): Sass and postcss-scss leave the engine, and the converter with them (#21217)

Nothing in the engine compiles or parses SCSS any more: the theme build copies plain CSS,
and the scaffolders, lints and move tooling parse with postcss. `npm ls sass postcss-scss`
on the lockfile is empty. The converter needed both and leaves with them; the Institution's
and the private package's conversions run it from 9955e13cc6.

* test(themes): three component specs load the neo themes' tokens from their Global sheet (#21217)

Chip, tab ContainerUi and DragProxyDensity loaded the standalone design-token sheets by
path; those sheets left in 5d1814710f, and the tokens live in each neo theme's Global.css.
17 of 17 pass locally.

* feat(portal): the examples open on a groups overview, phase 1 (#21130)

What both desktop controls share, per the ticket's Fix:

- `/examples` opens an overview: the headline counts what the selected
  build publishes, the action tests its first claim, three groups to
  start with, the banded index, and every group's card by band.
- The banded index is one component, `Portal.view.examples.GroupIndex`,
  bound to the new groups store, in three presentations: the overview,
  a group page's desktop control (phase 2), the phone's sheet.
- A group counts its home records, so the counts add up to the headline.
  A group that only borrows cards shows them in parentheses, explained
  under the index.
- Below 640 px a group page keeps a crumb whose group button opens the
  full index as a sheet: it takes focus, closes on Escape and returns
  focus to the button.
- The section is no longer a tab container. `TabContainer` becomes
  `MainContainer`, a card layout over the overview and one page per
  published group. Inactive cards stay in the DOM, so each page keeps
  its scroll position. The overview replaces the Featured list, as on
  the design board.

spec-retired: test/playwright/unit/apps/portal/view/examples/TabContainerController.spec.mjs moves to MainContainerController.spec.mjs with the controller it tests

* fix(portal): the phone overview hides its start cards, whichever sheet loads last (#21130)

The list's own `display: grid` has the same specificity as the phone
rule that hides the start cards, so the later sheet won and the index
fell below two screens at 390x664. The e2e arm for the group cards
waits for the web font before it measures a caption.

* test(portal): the examples e2e reads a settled section (#21130)

closes its menu, and a card left by the pointer closes its action line
over a transition. The arms now wait for one visible page, a closed
menu and the resting card, and the card check names the cards that
miss it. Locally 19 of 22 arms pass; three stay open on the PR.

* test(portal): the examples e2e waits for the page a reader sees (#21130)

The three open arms read the section in the middle of a card switch. The card
layout keeps inactive cards mounted here, and it flips the hidden and the
shown card in two component updates. After a sheet link the old page still
had an update in flight, so both pages showed at once and the heading
locator matched two. The shared-catalog arm clicked the build control before
the overview was back, and the Workstation arm read the Multi-Window list
before the catalog had created its page.

expectOpenPage() waits until the named page is the only one that shows, and
openOverview() until no page shows. The catalog and Connect specs pass 22 of
22, twice in full-file runs.

* feat(portal): a group page reaches the other groups by the upright index or the switcher (#21130)

Phase 2, the desktop control that OQ3 of Discussion #20742 still has to
pick. MainContainer#groupControl sets it on every page:

- list, the default and the design seat's pick: the banded index stands
  upright beside the heading and the cards, and ends above the fold of a
  720 px viewport (at 693 px for 1280x720).
- switcher, the operator's recorded preference: the crumb shows at every
  width, its group button is a pill naming how many groups the selected
  build publishes, and a link to the next group ends the cards (GroupIndex
  presentation next; after the last group it leads to the overview).

Below 640 px both keep the crumb's sheet. No card is narrower than 410 px:
two columns of 562 px beside the index at 1440x900, three of about 450 px
with the switcher.

The page places its five items on a CSS grid instead of nesting them, so the
cards stay a direct child of the page that scrolls, the root of their
intersection observer. Its rows are max-content: with auto rows the
overflowing page left no free space, and the header, which clips, shrank to
its padding under the cards. List#onIntersect now returns for a record that
a build switch dropped (a TypeError in the App Worker during the counts arm).

The config and the control the ruling does not pick leave the pull request
with that ruling.
